age-of-acquisition-influence-on-the-pre-: How early in life you learned an object does not change how fast or accurately you decide which group it belongs to.
anchoring-effect: People's estimates of a number stay too close to a starting number they were given or thought of first.
better-than-chance-recognition-of-old-ob: People can pick out an object they saw earlier when it is shown next to a new one, better than guessing.
framing: Pre-selecting an option, or wording a choice as opting in versus opting out, changes what people end up choosing.
frequency-influence-on-the-conceptual-st: How common an object's name is does not change how quickly people write that name when shown its picture.
gaze-following-in-domesticated-pigs: Pigs do not use the direction a person is looking to choose between objects and find a reward.
hybrid-entrepreneurship-and-psychologica: People running a business alongside a job show a distinct pattern of well-being, shaped by who chooses that path.
lexical-precision-on-lexical-competition: A barely seen flash of a similar-looking word changes how fast people read a word, depending on their spelling skill.
numerical-ratio-effects-on-quantity-disc: Elephants' ability to pick the larger of two amounts does not depend on how close the two amounts are.
positive-affirmation-on-mood: Telling yourself positive things can fail to lift your mood or even make you feel worse.
reasoning-about-hidden-causal-agents-in-: Crows become warier when a stick moves with no person seen, as if reasoning that someone is hidden nearby.
syntactic-predictability-in-older-adults: Older adults read a sentence more easily when it includes the word "either", which helps them predict what comes next.
temporal-doppler-effect: People sense that past events are further away from now than future events are.
